headline: Bangladesh to add 1,600mmcfd LNG capacity by 2030 to meet rising demand
summary: State Minister Aninda Islam Amit reveals plans for new floating and land-based terminals to reduce reliance on domestic gas as production falls short.
details: Bangladesh plans to increase its LNG regasification capacity by 1,600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) by 2030. This move comes as domestic gas production continues to fall short of the country's growing energy needs.
The expansion will include a 600mmcfd floating LNG terminal at Moheshkhali by 2028 and a 1,000mmcfd land-based terminal at Matarbari by 2030.
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit announced these plans during the 15th LNG Producer-Consumer Conference in Tokyo, Japan.
Currently, Bangladesh operates two floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) supplying approximately 1,100mmcfd of gas, with an annual LNG requirement of around 7 million tonnes.
The State Minister noted that LNG requirements could increase by 3-4 million tonnes per annum between 2026 and 2030, potentially reaching 17-18 million tonnes per annum by 2040.
To secure this supply, the government will use government-to-government deals, international requests for quotations, and direct procurement, while seeking international investment.
Additionally, the government is launching an offshore bidding round for 2026 to attract investment for domestic oil and gas exploration to diversify energy sources.
caption:
Bangladesh is scaling up its energy infrastructure to secure its future. 1,600mmcfd of new LNG capacity is coming by 2030.

Bangladesh plans to increase its LNG regasification capacity by 1,600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) by 2030. This move comes as domestic gas production continues to fall short of the country's growing energy needs.

The expansion will include a 600mmcfd floating LNG terminal at Moheshkhali by 2028 and a 1,000mmcfd land-based terminal at Matarbari by 2030.

State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit announced these plans during the 15th LNG Producer-Consumer Conference in Tokyo, Japan.

Currently, Bangladesh operates two floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) supplying approximately 1,100mmcfd of gas, with an annual LNG requirement of around 7 million tonnes.

The State Minister noted that LNG requirements could increase by 3-4 million tonnes per annum between 2026 and 2030, potentially reaching 17-18 million tonnes per annum by 2040.

To secure this supply, the government will use government-to-government deals, international requests for quotations, and direct procurement, while seeking international investment.

Additionally, the government is launching an offshore bidding round for 2026 to attract investment for domestic oil and gas exploration to diversify energy sources.

headline: Woman's dismembered body found in suitcase under Gazipur culvert
summary: Police recovered the remains of an unidentified woman, aged 30-35, from a suitcase and sacks near the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.
details: Police recovered the dismembered and partially decomposed body of an unidentified woman from a blue suitcase under a culvert in the Bhabanipur area of Joydebpur, Gazipur.
Local residents discovered the suitcase near Fikira Garments on Friday afternoon and alerted the authorities.
Following the initial discovery, police conducted a search in the surrounding area and found other body parts packed in sacks.
The remains have been sent to Gazipur Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College morgue for a post-mortem examination.
Joydebpur Police Station OC Al Mamun stated the victim is estimated to be between 30 and 35 years old, but her identity remains unknown due to the state of the body.
Police suspect the woman was murdered elsewhere, and her body was subsequently dismembered and dumped at the location to hide the crime.
caption:

Joydebpur Police Station OC Al Mamun stated the victim is estimated to be between 30 and 35 years old, but her identity remains unknown due to the state of the body.
